title: Brownies
subtitle: Serves 12
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan.
Add the chocolate and stir until fully combined, then remove from heat.
Add the sugar and stir.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and let it cool slightly.
Add the eggs and stir.
Fold in the flour and a pinch of salt.
Fold in the walnuts.
Pour the batter into a baking pan.
Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes.
doneness: It's ready when a toothpick comes out almost clean.
note: You can melt the butter and chocolate together in the microwave in short bursts, stirring each time.

title: Pancakes
subtitle: Makes about 15
steps: Add the eggs, vanilla, milk and water to the flour, salt and baking powder, and beat until smooth.
Place the batter in a sealed container and leave to stand overnight before cooking.
note: The source notes only cover mixing the batter — worth asking Mom how she actually cooks these on the pan (heat, timing, when to flip) to fill in the missing step.

title: Red Velvet Cupcakes
subtitle: Makes 12

ingredients.text: Frosting: 1/2 cup unsalted butter, room temp
Frosting: 4 oz cream cheese, room temp

steps: Preheat the oven and line a muffin pan.
Whisk the dry ingredients (flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder, sugar, salt) together in one bowl.
In a separate bowl whisk the wet ingredients (buttermilk, oil, egg, vinegar, vanilla, food coloring), then combine with the dry mix until smooth.
Fill liners 2/3 full, bake 18–20 min until they spring back when pressed. Cool fully before frosting.
For the frosting: beat the butter, cream cheese, salt and vanilla until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time. Loosen with a splash of milk if too thick.
note: Anna Olson's version swaps the food coloring for grated raw beets — more natural, a softer pink-red instead of vivid red. Worth trying as an old-fashioned variant.

title: Irish Scones
subtitle: Makes 12
steps: Add the flour to a large bowl. Grate the frozen butter straight into it — this is the key trick, cold butter creates flaky pockets as it bakes.
Stir in the sugar, baking powder and raisins.
Whisk the eggs and milk together, pour into the flour mixture, and stir until a soft dough just comes together.
Turn out onto a floured surface, press to about 1 inch thick, cut into rounds with a 3-inch cutter, gather scraps and repeat.
Brush tops with egg wash, bake 22–26 minutes until golden brown.
Cool slightly, then serve with butter, jam, and/or clotted cream.
note: Serve with butter, jam, and/or clotted cream.

title: Stovetop Popcorn
subtitle: About 10 cups

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil or coconut oil

steps: Heat the oil with 2 kernels in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat, lid on. Wait for those 2 to pop — that's your signal the oil's ready.
Remove from heat, add the remaining kernels, cover, shimmy to spread evenly, and let sit 60 seconds off the heat.
Return to medium heat, shimmying occasionally. Once popping starts, crack the lid slightly to let steam escape.
Cook until pops slow to a few seconds apart. Tip into a bowl, salt to taste, serve right away.
note: Don't crank the heat too high — if you ever see real smoke, turn off the heat and leave the lid on rather than moving the pot.

title: Spicy Orange Bran Muffins
steps: Combine the bran and buttermilk, let it sit while you prep everything else to soften the bran.
In one bowl combine the remaining dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, raisins, zest).
In another bowl whisk the egg, brown sugar, honey, molasses and oil together.
Stir in the bran mixture, then the dry ingredients, just until combined.
Bake in a greased muffin tin at 375°F for about 20 minutes. Best served warm.

title: Orange Muffins (Buttermilk by Sam)
subtitle: Makes 12
steps: Rub the sugar and orange zest together to release the oils.
Beat in the eggs until light and fluffy, then slowly drizzle in the oil.
Fold in the flour, vanilla, salt and baking soda, then mix in the kefir and orange juice.
Chill the batter 2–4 hours (or overnight) for a better rise.
Bake in alternating muffin cups, so they're not touching, at 400°F for about 18 minutes.
Dip cooled muffins in glaze, or sprinkle with sugar before baking.
note: 1 cup powdered sugar + 3 tbsp orange juice + pinch of salt + dash of vanilla.

title: Orange Muffins (Pretty. Simple. Sweet.)
subtitle: Makes 12

ingredients.text: 1/3 cup (75g) melted unsalted butter or neutral oil
1 cup optional add-ins (chocolate chips, berries, raisins, nuts)

steps: Toss the sugar and zest together to release the orange oils, then mix in the flour, baking powder and salt.
In a separate bowl whisk the eggs, melted butter, sour cream, milk, orange juice and vanilla.
Combine the wet mixture into the dry just until mixed, then fold in any add-ins.
Bake 15–20 minutes at 375°F until a toothpick comes out clean.
Drizzle with glaze once cooled, if using.
note: 1/2 cup powdered sugar + 1–2 tbsp orange juice.

title: Banana Cinnamon Muffins
subtitle: Makes 12
steps: Sift the flour, baking powder, bicarb, salt and cinnamon together; stir in the sugar and orange rind.
Whisk the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla together.
Add the wet mixture to the dry, alternating with the mashed banana, mixing lightly — don't overmix, the batter should stay a bit lumpy.
Spoon into greased muffin pans, filling 2/3 full. Bake at 180°C for 20–25 minutes until golden. Cool on a wire rack; serve warm with butter.

title: Cinnamon Snackers
subtitle: Makes about 20
steps: Cream the butter and sugar, beat in the egg and vanilla until light.
Sift the flour and salt (add back any bran caught in the sieve) and mix in to form a soft dough.
Mix the topping sugar and cinnamon together. Roll the dough into small balls, then roll each ball in the cinnamon-sugar.
Place on a greased tray, flatten lightly with a fork, and bake at 180°C for 10–12 minutes. Cool on a wire rack, store in an airtight container.

title: Instant Pot Sweet Potatoes
steps: Pressure-cook whole sweet potatoes, then allow a 10 minute natural release. Timing depends on size:
Small (under 2 in wide): 15 minutes.
Medium (2–3 in wide): 30 minutes.
Large (3–4 in wide): 60 minutes.
note: This is Mom's own timing reference, not a full recipe.

title: Banana Loaf
subtitle: Loaf or ~12 cupcakes

ingredients.text: 1 cup sugar (quantity uncertain — confirm with Mom)
Milk (amount not specified on the card)

steps: Cream the butter and sugar, then add the well-beaten eggs.
Mix the eggs with a bit of milk.
Fold in the flour mixed with the baking powder and bicarb.
Add the mashed bananas and bake in a medium oven — 1 hour at 180°C as a loaf, or about 30 minutes as cupcakes.
doneness: TBD — the sugar quantity and whether there's a pinch of salt were hard to read on the original card. Double-check with Mom, or she may remember the amounts by heart.
note: Mom swapped the milk for buttermilk once and said it worked really well — she also used 6 small bananas instead of 4 medium, which made the loaf noticeably higher. (Dated 30/4/2024)

title: Vegetable Breyani

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp ground whole spice (garam masala), fried briefly in oil
6 small pieces of butter, for steaming

steps: Fry the ground whole spice briefly in oil, then add the onions, cumin seeds and halved green chili. Fry until golden, about 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger, salt, Kokni, cumin, coriander and turmeric. Add a dash of boiled water to help cook the spices through.
Add the cauliflower, broccoli and stir-fry vegetables. Toss with the onion mixture briefly.
Add 1/2 cup water and cook for about 20 minutes, until the vegetables are soft.
Separately, cook the basmati rice with the ghee, cinnamon stick, 2 tsp salt and a little turmeric.

To assemble: layer the vegetable-and-onion mixture, then the drained lentils and butter beans, then the rice on top. Dot the top with the 6 small pieces of butter, close the lid, and steam over very low heat for 20 minutes — same method as the chicken breyani.

title: Muesli
steps: Mix the almonds, raw cocoa, coconut shavings, pumpkin seeds and sunflower seeds in a bowl.
Add the cocoa powder and stir in the coconut oil to coat.
Spread out and bake at 150°C, stirring regularly so it toasts evenly.

title: Date Slices

ingredients.text: Water, enough to mix with the dates

steps: Mix the dates with a little water and the butter, then stir in the crushed cranberries.
Add the almonds, flour, Pronutro and a little bicarb.
Mix and spread into an oven pan, then bake. No time or temp was noted on this one — worth checking with Mom, or test at a standard 180°C and watch for golden edges.

title: Barley and Raisin Water
steps: Soak the barley overnight, rinse, then soak again.
Boil the barley, adding the raisins towards the end of the process.

title: Lamb Pilaf

ingredients.text: 2 beef stock cubes, dissolved in 750ml water
Steak and chips spice, for the meat

steps: Boil the rice.
Sprinkle the lamb with steak and chips spice, then brown the meat and trim off excess fat.
Place the lamb in a pressure cooker for 30 minutes.
Fry the onions, chilies, garlic-ginger mix, cinnamon stick, and spices (Kokni, cumin, turmeric, oregano) to build the onion mixture, using the beef stock as needed.
Add the cooked lamb to the onion mixture, then stir through the lentils.
Combine with the boiled rice, season with salt and pepper to taste.

title: Macaroni and Cheese

ingredients.text: A bunch of celery, finely chopped

steps: Boil the macaroni in the water with the 15ml salt until done.
In a pan, cook the onions, celery and green pepper in the 100g butter until soft and golden. Stir in the Nando's mild sauce.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the origanum, paprika and mustard.
In an oven dish, combine the cooked macaroni, breadcrumbs, grated cheese and the onion mixture.
Whisk the eggs with the 2 tsp salt and the milk, then pour over everything in the dish.
Bake at 180°C for 1 hour. Cool before serving.

title: Chicken Pilaf

ingredients.text: 1 tsp chicken stock, dissolved in 750ml water

steps: Boil the rice.
Sprinkle the chicken with chicken spice, then brown it and trim off excess fat.
Melt the butter in a pot, add diced onions, chili, garlic and ginger, and cook until soft and golden.
Stir in the masala/Kokni, oregano, turmeric and cumin. Add a splash of boiling water and cook for about a minute to bring out the spices.
Add the browned chicken, stir, season with salt and pepper, then add the stock. Cook for about 5 minutes.
Stir in the lentils.
Mix the chicken mixture into the boiled rice. Cover the dish with foil and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.

title: Chicken and Creamed Corn Soup

ingredients.text: Chicken spice, Cajun spice, oregano, salt and pepper, to season
2 cups half and half (1 cup cream + 1 cup milk)
Cayenne pepper, salt (generously) and pepper, to taste
Cream of corn "cuppa soup" sachets, sifted

steps: In a small pot, cook the diced red onion, mashed garlic and chili flakes.
Season the cubed chicken with chicken spice, Cajun spice, oregano, salt and pepper. Cook until browned, then let it rest with the lid on.

Separately, make the creamed corn: melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add the half-and-half. Season with cayenne pepper, salt and pepper. Add the frozen corn and bring to a boil, about 10 minutes, then simmer for 15 minutes.
For the stock: combine the boiling water with the sifted cream-of-corn soup sachet and the chicken stock.
Combine the chicken, creamed corn and stock together in one pot, and boil for a few minutes. Finish with fresh parsley.

title: Christmas Cake
subtitle: Serves 20–25

ingredients.text: 1 cup + 2 tbsp apple juice (or 1/3 brandy + 2/3 apple juice)

steps: Combine the dried fruit and juice/brandy in a microwavable container. Microwave for about 1.5 minutes until hot, stir to coat, then cover and let sit for 1 hour to plump up and cool.
Preheat oven to 160°C (140°C fan). Grease and line a deep 21–22cm round cake tin.
Beat the butter and sugar until smooth. Beat in the oil and molasses.
Add the salt, spices and baking powder, beat to combine. Add the eggs one at a time, beating just until incorporated.
Stir in the flour, then fold in the soaked fruit (with any remaining liquid) and the walnuts.
Pour into the tin, cover with foil, and bake 2.5 hours. Remove the foil and bake a further 30–45 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool 20 minutes in the tin, then transfer to a rack to cool completely before serving or decorating.
note: Keeps well — a few months in the fridge, about a year in the freezer.
